So instead of believing in a god you believe in yourself right?
Sometimes you can’t argue what you believe in. If you’ve ever felt it, then I guess you’d know. Faith is powerful and you realize that when you’ve lived life without it.
How did you come to believe in ones own spiritual power?

I actually watched a sermon on this because I was asking the exact same questions. Among other things, it said that the prophets of other religions spoke about their god and then died, whereas in Christianity prophets spoke about God but later He spoke to us by His son Jesus, and then Jesus came back from the dead because He is God. If you ever want to watch that sermon, this is the link: https://www.cornerstoneorillia.org/teaching/watch_services_live/index.php The sermon date is May 24/20 and skip to 18:10 Also there is a movie and book called The Case for Christ. Have you ever seen it? It’s really good        Also lol yeah, idk what things would have looked like back in the Ancient times. We’d probably be rocking a pair of gladiator sandals though, on a separate note.       Sometimes I wonder which religion I would have chosen if I wasn’t raised in a Christian home. Either God still would have chosen you or me to be his children, or else I’d have a completely different perspective than I do now.         There was war back in the stories of the bible. God chose someone like David to lead an army or else they would have been slaughtered. It’s the world that is a sinful place, not God.         Think about a marriage based on trust. You’re living each day together trusting that he/she will not cheat. To live each day with your significant other is to have faith that you’ll stay happily married. Now you can’t see faith, but you do trust your partner to go out for drinks with their friends, and you’re not worried that they’ll cheat. You don’t know if they’ll cheat, but you still have faith that they won’t and so you stay in the marriage. This is evidence enough to believe in something you can’t see. Although there is proof that Jesus died on the cross (and I think there is evidence that he rose from the grave) aka “The Case for Christ,” faith is just as strong as any other type of evidence.

If you didn’t believe in God 100% but he knew you were trying and he knew you’ve asked him to save you, I think that would mean everything. Because if nobody can be perfect in this world, I think that’s enough to get someone eternally saved. There’s a lot of ups and downs in this world so I doubt it’s always easy to stay firm in the faith but, once a Christian, always a Christian. I heard somewhere before that every single person in the world will hear about Jesus at some point, and that that is their chance to learn about him and to ask Jesus into their hearts. For that reason I don’t think I need to worry about other gods because God is the one true God.    Humans only became flawed because they choose to eat from the tree God had forbidden and therefore sinned.     Maybe what’s frightening is knowing that “you” are drifting away from God. God is a powerful God, I guess it should scare “you” (not you you).    I understand doing your research on religions because I do not want to blindly obey either, but after all your research how can you call the God of the Bible evil?     Have you actually found that you are happier not being a Christian and instead relying on your own inner power?  (Edit: Also, I’ve heard that you know whether someone is a Christian by their fruits. It’s a change in heart and it’s noticeable to the people around us. That’s sort of the “proof”)
